stemMd: Why is removing a second electron from sodium much harder than removing its first?

options.label: A
options.textMd: The sodium nucleus loses all protons after first ionisation.

options.label: B
options.textMd: The second electron would be removed from a filled inner shell of the sodium ion.

options.label: C
options.textMd: The first electron has negative mass.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The second electron has no attraction to the nucleus.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Sodium becomes a different element after losing one electron.

explanationMd: The first ionisation removes the outer valence electron. The resulting ion has a closed shell; removing a further electron disrupts that more tightly bound configuration, causing a large energy jump.

distractorRationale.c: Electron mass does not explain the jump.
distractorRationale.d: It is more strongly bound, not unbound.
distractorRationale.a: Ionisation changes electrons, not the nucleus.
